segments.text: Ganymede, Jupiter's biggest moon, is the largest moon in the whole solar system.
segments.headline: The biggest moon

segments.text: It's about five thousand two hundred and seventy kilometers wide. That's bigger than the planet Mercury.
And it's the only moon we know that makes its own magnetic field. So Ganymede has its own auroras.
segments.headline: Its own auroras

segments.text: In twenty fifteen, Hubble watched those auroras rock back and forth. A huge salty ocean under the ice was holding them steady.
segments.headline: An ocean underneath

segments.text: That ocean, buried under about one hundred and fifty kilometers of ice, may hold more water than all the oceans on Earth.
Its surface is a patchwork: dark ancient ground, crossed by bright grooves where the ice cracked and shifted.
segments.headline: Cracked ice

segments.text: In twenty twenty-three, Europe launched a spacecraft called Juice. It reaches Jupiter in twenty thirty-one.
segments.headline: Juice is on its way

segments.text: In twenty thirty-four, it will orbit Ganymede. The first spacecraft ever to orbit a moon other than our own.
But Jupiter's next moon out has the oldest face in the solar system. Covered in craters, and almost unchanged for four billion years. Follow, so you don't miss episode ninety-four.
